subject: Invoice routing for renewal — EU subsidiary split + overage allocation
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@finicity.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Moran <lisa.moran@finicity.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal invoice routing question — splitting EU billing and PO submission

Hi Olga,

We received the renewal/upsell quote for our enterprise account and need to confirm invoice routing and PO handling before we route this to Treasury. Two items to confirm:

1) We need the invoice split between Finicity US (parent) and our EU subsidiary (Finicity EU S.à r.l.). Can Redwood issue two invoices each billing period, one to the US legal entity and one to the EU entity?

2) Our procurement team will issue a PO but it needs to reference the correct billing entities and net terms. Please confirm which net terms you will accept for the renewal amendment (we typically do net60). We also need to know the exact invoice recipient lines and any tax form requirements for the EU entity (W8/W9 equivalent).

We can attach the PO once we have the invoice lines confirmed. Please loop in finance if needed.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Finicity, Inc.
procurement@finicity.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@finicity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal invoice routing question — splitting EU billing and PO submission

Hi — thanks for the note and congrats on the renewal. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Yes, we can issue two invoices (US parent + EU subsidiary) on a recurring basis. Finance will create separate invoice recipients tied to the entities you provide.
- Our standard commercial accepts net45 on hosted product renewals; for deals with multi-entity billing we can review net60 but would need Treasury approval.
- For the EU entity we require a local tax identifier (EUID or VAT ID) and a completed W-8 BEN-E (or equivalent local tax form) for record keeping. If the EU entity is VAT-registered, please include the VAT number and indicate reverse charge applicability if relevant.

Please attach the PO and the EU entity legal name, billing address, VAT/EIN, and the contact email for accounts-payable at the EU entity. I'll loop Finance on this thread (cc'd).

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Manager, Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@finicity.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal invoice routing question — splitting EU billing and PO submission

Hi Lisa / Procurement team,

Kimberly from Finance here. A few clarifications from the billing side so we can process the PO quickly: 

- We can set up two invoice recipients: Finicity, Inc. (US) and Finicity EU S.à r.l. (EU). Each recipient will receive a separate invoice for its portion of the commitment and any usage-based overages tied to that entity.
- Net terms: our default for multi-entity split billing is net45. We will accept net60 for this renewal if Treasury confirms; please let us know if internal approvals will take a week or more.
- Attach the PO to this thread and ensure the PO line explicitly states which entity is responsible for each SKU/commitment block. If the PO is for the parent but you want invoices split, include a billing allocation table as an attachment (example: 70% parent / 30% EU).
- Tax forms: for the EU entity we need the VAT number and a completed W-8 BEN-E if the entity is a non-US withholding entity; attach any local tax certificate if available.

Once we have the PO and tax id, we'll provision two invoice recipients and send a draft invoice template for review. If overage fees are expected during the first quarter after upgrade, let us know how you'd like those charged (charged to the entity that incurred the usage vs. pooled to parent).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Lisa Moran <lisa.moran@finicity.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finicity.com>, Finicity Treasury <treasury@finicity.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal invoice routing question — splitting EU billing and PO submission

Hi Olga / Kimberly — attaching the PO and tax docs per your request.

Attachments: Finicity_PO_7892.pdf (PO), Finicity_W8BEN-E.pdf (EU subsidiary tax form)

Summary:
- PO 7892: includes two line items — Core Commit (assign to US parent) and Additional EU Capacity (assign to Finicity EU S.à r.l.). PO explicitly calls out allocation: 65% US / 35% EU.
- Finicity EU S.à r.l. VAT: LU12345678 (please confirm how that should appear on the invoice).
- Treasury prefers net60 for this cycle; they can approve if Redwood is able to accept net60 for the EU entity.
- Please confirm whether you will bill overage fees to the entity that incurs them (recommended) or pool to the parent.

Let me know if the attachments didn't come through.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Moran
Head of Procurement
Finicity, Inc.
lisa.moran@finicity.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Moran <lisa.moran@finicity.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal invoice routing question — splitting EU billing and PO submission

Lisa — got the PO and W-8 BEN-E, thank you. Kimberly — finance has the docs; can you confirm net60 for the EU entity? If OK, we will accept net60 for the EU invoice only and keep net45 for the US parent (we'll note the exception on the renewal amendment).

Marissa — looping you in to confirm how we should reflect the overage allocation in the amendment and whether we want to surface any estimated prorated credits for the mid-term capacity bump. My suggestion: charge overages to the entity that generated them (match allocation on the PO) to simplify treasury reconciliation, and include a brief schedule in the amendment showing allocation percentages.

If everyone agrees I'll kick off the amendment DocuSign and provision the two invoice recipients so we can test a sample invoice PDF.

Best,
Olga
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Lisa Moran <lisa.moran@finicity.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal invoice routing question — splitting EU billing and PO submission

Thanks all — quick plan and next steps from Account side: 

1) Finance confirmed: we can accept net60 for the EU recipient as a one-time exception for this renewal. Kimberly, please confirm final approval but we expect yes.
2) Overage fees: we will bill overages to the entity that incurred usage. We'll include an allocation table in the amendment matching the PO (65% US / 35% EU).
3) I will prepare the amendment (term addendum + invoice-recipient table) and send via DocuSign for signatures. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/finicity-amendment-8921
4) Olga — once signed, please provision the two invoice recipients and upload the sample invoice PDF here for Finicity to verify layout.

Lisa — thanks for the PO and W-8. Expect the DocuSign within 24 hours.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
